stances.claim: The electorate won -- not either Robredo or Marcos -- because the PET moved away from arbitrary numerical thresholds toward a method that actually mimics how VCMs counted votes during the election, using Election Returns as the guide.

The PET's original 50% threshold was correct given the 2010 calibration -- and the later correction to 20-25% was equally principled, showing the Tribunal was responsive to official Comelec data rather than partisan pressure.
stances.rhetorical_move: institutional-principle vindication (both thresholds were principled in their context)

stances.claim: The ER-guided method is superior to both re-feeding (technically impractical) and digital ballot images (extremely tedious), and better reflects the actual election outcome.
stances.rhetorical_move: three-option comparative analysis selecting the least-burdensome technically sound method

notable_anecdotes: The practical example in the PET resolution -- if ER shows 395 votes but physical count shows 398, head revisor reports 395 and the 3 stray ballots are for PET appreciation -- making abstract procedure concrete.
Both Robredo and Marcos claiming victory in the same unanimous resolution -- CJ immediately reframes by declaring a third winner: 'the electorate.'
The SD card technical challenge preventing VCM re-feeding -- a hardware constraint that forced the PET to devise the ER-guided alternative, illustrating how technical realities shape legal procedure.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes the Presidential Electoral Tribunal's unanimous September 18, 2018 resolution (penned by Justice Caguioa) on the VP electoral protest's 'shading' controversy -- where Robredo argued for a 25% threshold matching the 2016 VCM calibration while Marcos and Solicitor General Calida backed the PET Rules' 50% threshold based on the 2010 calibration. The PET originally denied Leni's motion because it had not yet been officially advised of the new calibration; after receiving the Comelec's July 18, 2018 comment confirming the 2016 VCMs were calibrated at a 20-25% range, the PET set aside the 50% threshold. Rather than use re-feeding (impractical due to SD card issues) or decrypted digital ballot images (extremely tedious), the PET directed head revisors to report vote counts as shown in the Election Returns generated by the VCMs -- with 'stray' ballots reserved for PET appreciation based on voter intent. CJ argues that while both Robredo and Marcos claimed victory, it is the electorate that won -- because the ER-guided mimicking method most faithfully reflects how VCMs actually counted votes during the 2016 election -- and that truth and logic won alongside.
